episodes.explanation: The Iberian market split on 22 September 2026 from 19:15Z to 20:00Z, with Portugal pricing 27.6 EUR/MWh higher than Spain at the worst interval (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead). At 19:45Z, the peak of the episode, Portugal reached 255.1 EUR/MWh while Spain stood at 227.5 EUR/MWh (ENTSO-E A44 day-ahead), and the scheduled flow from Spain to Portugal filled the available border capacity of 1,824 MW across all three settlement intervals in this 45-minute window (ENTSO-E A09 scheduled exchanges and A61 day-ahead capacity). The price separation cost importers 15,554.16 EUR on energy crossing the border at the higher Portuguese price (A44 prices with A09 scheduled flows). An unplanned outage on the Vermoim-Vila Nova Famalicão transmission asset left 1,824 MW available (ENTSO-E A78 transmission unavailability), and 13 notices were in force during the episode, with the most restrictive published on 22 September 2026 (ENTSO-E A78). The border being full is consistent with the price separation, though both follow from the same market coupling rather than one causing the other.

The extra import cost for energy crossing the border at the higher Portuguese price totalled 65,595.71 EUR (ENTSO-E A44 with A09 scheduled flows). Twelve transmission notices were in force during this period, published before the episode began, with six of them reporting the same remaining capacity constraint; the most restrictive notice was published on 27 July 2026 (ENTSO-E A78 transmission unavailability). The border being full is consistent with the price separation, though both outcomes follow from the same market coupling mechanism rather than one causing the other.
